args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks immediately after the v2.3.1 production deploy (error rate ~18%, unhealthy in us-east, us-west, and eu-west).

Action taken: Rolled the service back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production (v2.2.9 -> v2.3.0 -> v2.3.1; note v2.3.1-rc is a staging build and was also unhealthy, so it was not a rollback candidate).

The first rollback attempt failed partway (orchestrator error) with us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1. A retry completed the rollout.

Current state: all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) confirmed on v2.3.0 and healthy; error rate dropped to ~0.2%.

Follow-up: Root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures is not yet identified. v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until the failure is diagnosed and validated in staging.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
Done. The incident did get created despite the timeout, so I did not retry (avoiding a duplicate page).

**Summary:**

1. **Diagnosed:** `checkout-api` was on v2.3.1 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy, with an ~18% error rate — coinciding with the latest deploy.
2. **Chose rollback target:** Deployment history showed v2.2.9 (healthy) → v2.3.0 (healthy) → v2.3.1 (unhealthy). v2.3.1-rc was excluded as it's a staging build and was itself unhealthy. v2.3.0 is the most recent production-healthy release.
3. **Rolled back with a hiccup:** The first attempt failed partway with an orchestrator error — us-east moved to v2.3.0 but us-west and eu-west stayed on v2.3.1, leaving the service in a mixed, still-unhealthy state. A retry completed the rollout.
4. **Verified:** All three regions now on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate down to ~0.2%.
5. **Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2 for checkout-api, documenting the symptoms, the rollback (including the partial-failure/retry), and the current verified state.

Note: the `create_incident` call returned a timeout error, but a follow-up `list_incidents` confirmed INC-0001 exists and is open — no duplicate was created.

**Follow-up worth flagging:** the root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures isn't identified. v2.3.1 (and v2.3.1-rc behind it) shouldn't be redeployed until that's diagnosed and validated in staging. No approval-gated actions were needed here since rolling back to a previously production-healthy version isn't covered by the change-manager policy.
